public_rationale: Reuters reported a 2025 cash-burn target of $8.5 billion on September 29, 2025 [e1]. The Next Web reported on September 19, 2026 that a July 2026 projection put cumulative negative free cash flow for 2026–2030 at $278 billion [e2]. These projections establish neither perpetual future cash burn nor a realized full year of positive free cash flow, so they leave the forecast unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: The cited annual and multiyear figures are projections, not realized cash-flow results [e1, e2].
Reuters could not independently verify the underlying report [e1].
Neither item provides reconciled operating cash flow and capital expenditure establishing a qualifying positive-free-cash-flow year [e1, e2].
No finite history of cash burn can establish perpetual future burn.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will continue burning money indefinitely.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI burned $5 billion in 2024, will likely burn $11 billion in 2025, and will continue burning money in perpetuity

from_speaker: will continue burning money in perpetuity
our_interpretation: Only the normalized perpetual-cash-burn forecast is graded here. The adjacent 2024 and 2025 figures are not separate claims in this item.

The ordinary financial reading of burning money is negative cash flow from operations and necessary investment, excluding financing inflows. Accounting losses and financing proceeds are not substitutes.

A full financial year of positive free cash flow from the continuing business would decisively contradict continued cash burn. This annual measurement period is an evaluator convention intended to exclude temporary cash timing effects.
No finite sequence of negative results establishes perpetual future cash burn.
criteria.support_condition: No finite reporting history can establish the forecast's unlimited future duration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable financial records establish a full financial year of positive free cash flow from OpenAI's continuing business, excluding financing proceeds and one-time asset disposals.
